parts.text: Write the HTML for a numbered list with these three items, in this order: 'Fill in the form', 'Upload a photograph', 'Pay the fee online'.
parts.answer:
1. Fill in the form
  2. Upload a photograph
  3. Pay the fee online
parts.working:
B1:
    …
; B1: each item in
  • …
    • ; B1: correct text in correct order.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the HTML for a paragraph containing the text 'Registration closes on 30 November.' with an inline style that makes the text colour #CC0000 and the font size 14pt.
parts.answer: Registration closes on 30 November.
parts.working: B1: style attribute in the opening p tag; B1: color: #CC0000; B1: font-size: 14pt; with correct punctuation and text.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the HTML for an internal stylesheet that makes every level 3 heading purple (#6A0DAD) and italic.
parts.answer:
<style>
h3 { color: #6A0DAD; font-style: italic; }
</style>
parts.working: B1: <style> … </style>; B1: h3 selector with color: #6A0DAD; B1: font-style: italic; with correct braces and punctuation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State where in the HTML document the internal stylesheet must be placed.
parts.answer: In the head section.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The image map.jpg is stored in a folder called img inside the folder that holds the web page. Write the HTML to display it 250 pixels high with its aspect ratio kept, and the alternative text 'Campus map'.
parts.working: B1: src="img/map.jpg" (relative path); B1: alt="Campus map"; B1: height="250" only (no width, so aspect ratio kept).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a CSS rule that gives every image on the page a solid border 4 pixels wide in the colour #8B4513.
parts.answer: img { border: 4px solid #8B4513; }
parts.working: B1: selector img and braces; B1: border property with 4px and solid; B1: #8B4513 and correct punctuation. Accept border-width/border-style/border-color as separate properties.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the purpose of each of these metatags: (i) description (ii) keywords (iii) author (iv) viewport.
parts.answer: (i) Gives a short summary of the page, which search engines may display in their results. (ii) Lists words that describe the page so search engines can match it to searches. (iii) Gives the name of the person who created the page. (iv) Tells the browser how to scale and size the page to fit the width of the device, so it displays correctly on phones and tablets.
parts.working: 1 mark for each correct purpose.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the purpose of the meta tag <meta charset="UTF-8">.
parts.answer: It tells the browser which character set to use so that text, including special characters, is displayed correctly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the presentation layer should be kept separate from the content layer by using an external stylesheet.
parts.answer: One stylesheet can be attached to every page, so all pages look consistent; changing one rule in the stylesheet updates every page at once; the HTML files are smaller and easier to read and edit because they contain only content; and different stylesheets can be used for different devices or for printing without changing the content.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four of: consistency across pages/house style | change once – updates all pages | saves time when restyling | HTML simpler/shorter/easier to maintain | faster loading – CSS cached once | different styles for different devices/print | developers and designers can work separately.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the <link> to an external stylesheet is placed in the head section.
parts.answer: The link is information about the page rather than content to display, so it belongs in the head; the head is read before the body is shown, so the styles are ready and the page is displayed correctly formatted from the start.
parts.working: B1: head holds information about the page/resources, not displayed content | loaded before the body so styles are applied when the page is shown.

practice.stem: A web page contains the hyperlink Sports news.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe what happens when a user clicks the words Sports news.
parts.answer: The browser opens the page sports.html from the news folder on www.example.org, and it opens in a new window or tab because of target="_blank".
parts.working: 1 mark: opens the sports.html page at that address. 1 mark: in a new tab/window.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between an absolute file path and a relative file path, and why relative paths are used for files within the same website.
parts.answer: An absolute path gives the full location from the root (e.g. a full URL or a drive letter on the developer's computer); a relative path gives the location relative to the current page (e.g. images/logo.png). Relative paths keep working when the whole website is uploaded to a server or moved to another folder, whereas absolute local paths (such as C:\Users\...) would break.
parts.working: 1 mark: absolute – full path from root/drive/URL. 1 mark: relative – from the location of the current file. 1 mark: relative paths still work when the site is moved/uploaded; absolute local paths break.

practice.stem: A student describes the behaviour layer as 'the layer that makes the website look nice'.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the student is wrong and describe what the behaviour layer does.
parts.answer: Making the page look nice is the job of the presentation layer (CSS). The behaviour layer uses a scripting language (such as JavaScript) to make the page interactive – for example responding to button clicks, validating form entries or showing and hiding content.
parts.working: 1 mark: appearance is the presentation layer / CSS. 1 mark: behaviour layer uses scripts/scripting language. 1 mark: example of interactivity (validation, pop-ups, menus, responding to events).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why behaviour scripts are often kept in separate files.
parts.answer: The same script file can be used by many pages and changed in one place, keeping the HTML content simple.
parts.working: B1: reuse across pages | easier maintenance | content layer kept clean | cached by browser.

practice.stem: A photograph of Badshahi Mosque, mosque.png, is 1600 pixels wide and 1200 pixels high.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The image must be displayed 480 pixels wide with its aspect ratio maintained. Calculate the height in pixels.
parts.answer: 360 pixels

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the HTML to display the image at this size with alternative text 'Badshahi Mosque, Lahore'.
parts.working: 1 mark: src and alt correct. 1 mark: width 480 and height 360.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the image should also be resized in image-editing software before it is uploaded.
parts.answer: Setting width and height in HTML only changes how it is displayed; the full 1600 × 1200 file is still downloaded, so resizing the file itself reduces file size and makes the page load faster.
parts.working: 1 mark: HTML resizing does not reduce the file size. 1 mark: smaller file loads faster / uses less bandwidth.

practice.stem: A table must have this structure: row 1 has one cell spanning all three columns, containing the heading 'Exam Timetable'; row 2 has three header cells: Subject, Date, Time; row 3 has three data cells: Physics, 12 May, 09:00.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the HTML for this table.
parts.answer:
Exam Timetable
SubjectDateTime
Physics12 May09:00
parts.working:
1 mark: …
. 1 mark: three rows correctly closed. 1 mark: colspan="3" on the first cell. 1 mark: three cells in row 2. 1 mark: three data cells in row 3 with exact text. (Accept in row 1.)

parts.label: b
parts.text: State how a th cell normally appears differently from a td cell when no CSS is applied.
parts.answer: Text in a th (table header) cell is displayed bold and centred; text in a td cell is normal weight and left aligned.
parts.working: B1: th bold and centred (td plain, left aligned).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a CSS rule that makes all h2 headings: dark blue (#00008B), a sans-serif font with Arial as the first choice, 18 pt, centre aligned and italic.
parts.working: 1 mark each: color: #00008B | font-family: Arial, sans-serif (generic fallback last) | font-size: 18pt | text-align: center | font-style: italic. Selector h2 and braces required for full marks.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare a CSS class with an inline style for formatting part of a web page.
parts.answer: Both change the appearance of elements. parts.working: B1 each. COUNT counts the five numbers (12, 15, 0, 18, 9); COUNTA counts all seven non-empty cells.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the two values are different.
parts.answer: COUNT only counts cells containing numbers; COUNTA counts every cell that is not empty, including text such as 'absent'.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the value displayed by
(i) =2+3*4
(ii) =(2+3)*4
parts.working: 1 mark each (multiplication before addition; brackets first).

parts.label: b
parts.text: B2 contains 60 and C2 contains 80. A student enters =B2+C2/2 to find the mean of the two cells. State the value displayed and write the correct formula.
parts.working: B1: 60 + 40 = 100. 1 mark: correct formula.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sheet calculates the cost per student of a club using =B2/C2, where B2 holds the total cost and C2 the number of students. When C2 is 0 the cell shows #DIV/0!. Explain why.
parts.answer: The formula is trying to divide by zero, which cannot be calculated.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula that displays No students when C2 is 0 and otherwise shows the cost per student.
parts.answer: =IF(C2=0,"No students",B2/C2)
parts.working: 1 mark: IF testing C2=0 with "No students". 1 mark: B2/C2 as false value.

practice.stem: A student records the daily rainfall (mm) in Murree for 10 days in B2:B11: 0, 4.5, 0, 12, 0, 0, 7.2, 1.1, 0, 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a function to count the number of days on which some rain fell, and state its value.
parts.working: 1 mark function; B1: 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula to calculate the proportion of days with rain, using COUNTIF and COUNT, and state the result as a percentage.
parts.answer: =COUNTIF(B2:B11,">0")/COUNT(B2:B11); 50%
parts.working: 1 mark formula; B1: 5 ÷ 10 = 50%.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A sports coach keeps players' sprint times in a spreadsheet. Name the most suitable function for each task.
(i) Find the fastest (lowest) time.
(ii) Find how many times have been entered.
(iii) Find how many players are in the 'Under 16' group.
(iv) Show 'Selected' if a time is below 12 seconds, otherwise 'Not selected'.
parts.answer: (i) MIN (ii) COUNT (iii) COUNTIF (iv) IF
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem: A weather log in Quetta records the daily maximum temperature (°C) in cells B2 to B31 for one month.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in B33 that displays the highest temperature in B2:B31.
parts.answer: =MAX(B2:B31)
parts.working: 1 mark for =MAX(B2:B31).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula in B34 that displays the lowest temperature in B2:B31.
parts.answer: =MIN(B2:B31)
parts.working: 1 mark for =MIN(B2:B31).

practice.stem: Cell C5 contains the value 7.849.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value displayed by =ROUND(C5,1).
parts.working: 1 mark: rounds 7.849 to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed by =INT(C5).
parts.working: 1 mark: INT removes the decimal part.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the value displayed by =ROUNDUP(C5,0).
parts.working: 1 mark: rounds away from zero to a whole number.

practice.stem: Cell B2 contains 25 and cell C2 contains the text 'n/a'. Cell D2 contains the formula =B2+C2 and shows #VALUE!.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the cell shows #VALUE!.
parts.answer: The formula tries to add a number to text ('n/a'), which is not allowed.
parts.working: 1 mark: the cell contains text where a number is needed.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one way to make the formula ignore the text so that no error is shown.
parts.answer: Use =SUM(B2,C2) (SUM ignores text), or replace the text with a number or leave the cell blank, or use IF(ISNUMBER(C2),B2+C2,0).
parts.working: 1 mark for a valid method. Accept any suitable formula that ignores or handles the text.

practice.stem: A school attendance sheet has the words Present or Absent in cells D2 to D40, one for each pupil.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D42 that counts the number of cells in D2:D40 that contain the word Absent.
parts.answer: =COUNTIF(D2:D40,"Absent")
parts.working: 1 mark: COUNTIF function. 1 mark: the range D2:D40 and the criterion "Absent" in quotation marks.

practice.stem: Column A contains whole numbers. A teacher wants to check whether each number is even or odd.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in B2 that displays Even if the number in A2 is even and Odd if it is odd.
parts.answer: =IF(MOD(A2,2)=0,"Even","Odd")
parts.working: 1 mark: IF with a test on the remainder. 1 mark: MOD(A2,2)=0 with the correct text outputs.

practice.stem: Cell B2 contains the reading 42 and cell C2 contains the reading 57.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D2 that displays the difference between B2 and C2 as a positive number, whichever is larger.
parts.answer: =ABS(B2-C2)
parts.working: 1 mark: subtracts the two values. 1 mark: ABS gives a positive result.

practice.stem: A shop's stock sheet has the stock level for each item in column D.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in E2 that displays Reorder if the stock in D2 is less than 20, and OK otherwise.
parts.answer: =IF(D2<20,"Reorder","OK")
parts.working: 1 mark: IF with test D2<20. 1 mark: correct text in quotes for both outcomes.

practice.stem: Cell A1 contains 5, cell A2 contains the text 'ten' and cell A3 contains 7.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value displayed by =SUM(A1:A3).
parts.working: 1 mark: SUM ignores the text in A2, so 5 + 7 = 12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed by =AVERAGE(A1:A3).
parts.working: 1 mark: AVERAGE ignores the text, so (5 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6.

practice.stem: Cells B2 to B6 contain 12, 7, a blank cell, 19 and 4 (in that order).

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value displayed by =MIN(B2:B6).
parts.working: 1 mark: the blank cell is ignored, so the smallest number is 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what the error #NAME? means and give the most likely cause in this formula: =SUMM(B2:B8).
parts.answer: #NAME? means the spreadsheet does not recognise a name in the formula; the most likely cause is the misspelt function name (SUMM instead of SUM).
parts.working: 1 mark: the name is not recognised. 1 mark: the misspelt function name SUMM (or a missing quotation mark on text) and the correction to SUM.

practice.stem: An electronics shop stores the sales tax rate, 17%, in cell F1. Prices of items (Rs) are in B2 to B20.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to calculate the sales tax on the item in B2. It must give correct results when replicated down to C20.
parts.working: 1 mark: B2 multiplied by F1. 1 mark: F1 made absolute ($F$1). Accept =B2*F$1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why an absolute reference is needed in this formula.
parts.answer: When the formula is replicated, relative references change (B2 becomes B3, B4…) but the tax rate is always in F1, so the reference to F1 must not change; otherwise the formula would point to F2, F3… which are empty.
parts.working: 1 mark: relative references change when copied. 1 mark: F1 must stay fixed / would refer to empty cells.

parts.label: c
parts.text: B2 contains 2400 and B5 contains 1850. State the values displayed in C2 and C5.

practice.stem:
A soft-drinks distributor records sales (cartons). Column A holds the region and column B the sales.
Row 2: North | 1200
Row 3: South | 950
Row 4: North | 780
Row 5: East | 1430
Row 6: North | 610
Row 7: South | 1100

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the function to calculate the total sales for the North region.
parts.answer: =SUMIF(A2:A7,"North",B2:B7)
parts.working: 1 mark: SUMIF with criteria range A2:A7 and "North". 1 mark: sum range B2:B7.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the values that would be displayed for the total sales of North and of South.
parts.answer: North 2590; South 2050

practice.stem:
A spreadsheet holds quiz scores. Column A holds the class and column B the score.
Row 2: 10A | 72
Row 3: 10B | 65
Row 4: 10A | 88
Row 5: 10B | 59
Row 6: 10A | 64
Row 7: 10B | 81

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the function to calculate the mean score of class 10A.
parts.answer: =AVERAGEIF(A2:A7,"10A",B2:B7)
parts.working: 1 mark: AVERAGEIF with criteria range and "10A". 1 mark: average range B2:B7.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The result is rounded using =ROUND(AVERAGEIF(A2:A7,"10A",B2:B7),1). State the value displayed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the mean score of class 10B correct to 1 decimal place.

practice.stem:
A weather station's spreadsheet holds months in row 1 and rainfall (mm) in row 2.
B1:G1: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun
B2:G2: 23, 29, 41, 20, 22, 79

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a function that looks up and displays the rainfall for March from this table.
parts.answer: =HLOOKUP("Mar",B1:G2,2,FALSE)
parts.working: 1 mark: HLOOKUP with "Mar" (or a cell containing Mar). 1 mark: range B1:G2. 1 mark: row 2 and FALSE.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write a function to find the total rainfall for the six months and state its value.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Cell A1 contains 47.3681. State the value displayed by each formula.
(i) =ROUND(A1,2)
(ii) =ROUNDUP(A1,1)
(iii) =ROUNDDOWN(A1,2)
(iv) =INT(A1)
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A school in Faisalabad is taking 263 students on a trip. Each bus holds 45 students. The number of students is in B1 and the bus capacity in B2. Write a formula to calculate the number of buses needed, and state its value.
parts.answer: =ROUNDUP(B1/B2,0); 6
parts.working: 1 mark: ROUNDUP of B1/B2 to 0 places. B1: 263 ÷ 45 = 5.84… → 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: An egg farm collects 1000 eggs (in C1). A tray holds 30 eggs (in C2). Write a formula to calculate the number of full trays and state its value.
parts.answer: =ROUNDDOWN(C1/C2,0) (or =INT(C1/C2)); 33
parts.working: 1 mark: ROUNDDOWN or INT. B1: 33.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write a formula to calculate the number of eggs left over, using C1 and C2, and state its value.
parts.answer: =C1-ROUNDDOWN(C1/C2,0)*C2; 10
parts.working: 1 mark: valid formula with 10. Accept =MOD(C1,C2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cell B1 contains the exchange rate 278.50 (rupees per US dollar). The cell is given the name Rate. Write the formula in C5 to convert the dollar amount in B5 to rupees using the named cell.
parts.answer: =B5*Rate
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B5 contains 40. State the value displayed in C5.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two advantages of using a named range rather than the cell reference $B$1.
parts.answer: Any two: formulas are easier to read/understand; easier to enter without errors; the name acts as an absolute reference so it does not change when the formula is replicated; the range can be found/edited easily.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cell D2 contains the formula =B2*C2. It is replicated down to D5. Write the formula that will be in D5.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Cell E2 contains =D2*$G$1. It is replicated down to E5. Write the formula that will be in E5.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell referencing.
parts.answer: A relative reference changes to match its new position when the formula is copied/replicated. An absolute reference (with $ signs) always refers to the same cell however it is copied.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem:
A museum spreadsheet: column B holds visitors in 2024 and column C in 2025.
Row 2: Science gallery | 12500 | 14250
Row 3: Textile gallery | 8400 | 7980

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula for D2 to calculate the percentage change in visitors from 2024 to 2025.
parts.answer: =(C2-B2)/B2 (cell formatted as a percentage)
parts.working: 1 mark: (C2−B2) with brackets. 1 mark: divided by B2. Accept *100 if not formatted as percentage.

parts.label: b
parts.text: D2 and D3 are formatted as percentages to 1 decimal place. State the values displayed.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
B2 contains the population 1284567 and B3 contains 739421. State the value displayed by
(i) =ROUND(B2,-3)
(ii) =ROUND(B3,-3)
(iii) =ROUND(B2,-5)
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what the negative number in =ROUND(B2,-3) does.
parts.answer: It rounds to the left of the decimal point, here to the nearest thousand.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A school library records the number of pages of each book in cell B2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a nested IF formula for C2 that displays Long if the number of pages in B2 is more than 500, Medium if it is more than 200, and Short otherwise.
parts.answer: =IF(B2>500,"Long",IF(B2>200,"Medium","Short"))
parts.working: 1 mark: the first IF tests more than 500 pages. 1 mark: the second IF tests more than 200 inside the false branch. 1 mark: the final 'Short' text and correct quotation marks and brackets.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the label shown for books of 650, 500, 201 and 120 pages.
parts.answer: Long, Medium, Medium, Short
parts.working: 1 mark for 650 (Long) and 500 (Medium). 1 mark for 201 (Medium) and 120 (Short).

practice.stem: A courier charges Rs 150 per kg for parcels up to 5 kg, and Rs 100 for each extra kg above 5 kg. The weight of a parcel in kg is in cell B2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in C2 that calculates the shipping charge for the weight in B2.
parts.working: 1 mark: IF on weight up to 5 kg. 1 mark: Rs 150 × weight for up to 5 kg. 1 mark: 750 plus Rs 100 for each kg above 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the charge for a parcel of 3 kg and for a parcel of 8 kg.
parts.answer: Rs 450 for 3 kg; Rs 1050 for 8 kg

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D2 that displays Pass if the mark in B2 is at least 40 AND the attendance in C2 is at least 75; otherwise it displays Retake.
parts.answer: =IF(AND(B2>=40,C2>=75),"Pass","Retake")
parts.working: 1 mark: AND with both tests. 1 mark: correct outputs in quotation marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the output for each of these pairs (mark, attendance): (45, 80); (50, 70); (35, 90).
parts.answer: Pass; Retake; Retake
parts.working: 1 mark for the first pair (Pass). 1 mark for the other two (Retake).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D2 that displays Free if the age in B2 is 12 or under, or if the ticket type in C2 is Student; otherwise it displays Pay.
parts.answer: =IF(OR(B2<=12,C2="Student"),"Free","Pay")
parts.working: 1 mark: OR with both conditions. 1 mark: the text in quotes and the IF structure.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the output in D2 for these rows: age 9 and type Adult; age 30 and type Student; age 20 and type Adult.
parts.answer: Free; Free; Pay
parts.working: 1 mark for all three correct.

practice.stem: Cell A2 contains a total of minutes, such as 135, for a class project.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in C2 to display the whole number of hours, and a formula in D2 to display the minutes left over, for the number of minutes in A2.
parts.working: 1 mark: INT(A2/60) for whole hours. 1 mark: MOD(A2,60) for the remaining minutes. 1 mark: correct cell references with no decimal part.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the hours and minutes shown when A2 contains 135.
parts.answer: 2 hours and 15 minutes
parts.working: 1 mark: 135 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 15.

practice.stem: A bakery packs biscuits into boxes. The number of biscuits is in cell B2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in B3 that displays the number of boxes needed for the items in B2, if each box holds 12 items. The number of boxes must be a whole number that is rounded up.
parts.answer: =ROUNDUP(B2/12,0)
parts.working: 1 mark: divides the number of items by 12. 1 mark: ROUNDUP with 0 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the number of boxes displayed when B2 contains 100.
parts.working: 1 mark: 100 ÷ 12 = 8.33, rounded up to 9.

practice.stem: A bakery's sales sheet lists the product name in A2 to A60 and the sales value (Rs) for each row in B2 to B60.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula that totals the sales (Rs) for the product Cake only.
parts.answer: =SUMIF(A2:A60,"Cake",B2:B60)
parts.working: 1 mark: SUMIF. 1 mark: criterion range A2:A60, sum range B2:B60 and "Cake" in quotation marks.

practice.stem: A stationery shop has a price list in A2 to C40. Column A holds the product code, column B the name and column C the price (Rs).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a VLOOKUP formula in F2 that finds the price for the product code typed in E2. Use exact matching.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(E2,A2:C40,3,FALSE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with lookup value E2 and table A2:C40. 1 mark: column index 3 (price) and FALSE for exact match.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State what the formula displays if the code in E2 is not in the table.
parts.answer: #N/A
parts.working: 1 mark for #N/A (the code cannot be found).

practice.stem: Cells B2 to B20 hold test scores for a class. Several students were absent, so some of their cells are blank.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in B21 to calculate the average of the scores in B2 to B20.
parts.answer: =AVERAGE(B2:B20)
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State whether the blank cells are counted in the average, and explain your answer.
parts.answer: Blank cells are ignored, so they are not counted: AVERAGE divides the total by the number of cells that contain numbers.
parts.working: 1 mark: the blanks are not counted. 1 mark: the divisor is the number of numbers, not the number of cells.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in C2 that displays the share of the total as a percentage (B2 divided by the total of B2 to B6). Use an absolute reference so that the formula can be copied down to C6.
parts.working: 1 mark: divides B2 by the total. 1 mark: SUM over B2:B6. 1 mark: $B$2:$B$6 is absolute so the total does not change when copied.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value in C2 if B2 is 250 and the total of B2 to B6 is 1000, formatted as a percentage.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a single formula for C2 that displays the grade for the percentage in B2, using these boundaries: 80 or more A; 65 or more B; 50 or more C; below 50 U.
parts.working: 1 mark: first IF with B2>=80 → "A". 1 mark: nested IF for B. 1 mark: nested IF for C. 1 mark: "U" as final false value and correct brackets. Accept testing from lowest boundary with < in correct order.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the grades shown for the percentages 80, 79, 65, 50 and 49.5.
parts.answer: A, B, B, C, U
parts.working: 2 marks all correct; 1 mark for three or four correct.

practice.stem:
A courier company stores a lookup table in H2:J6.
Column H code | Column I city | Column J charge (Rs)
KHI | Karachi | 250
LHE | Lahore | 300
ISB | Islamabad | 350
PEW | Peshawar | 400
QTA | Quetta | 450
Orders are in rows 2 to 50; column B holds each order's city code.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to look up the delivery charge for the city code in B2. It must work when replicated down column C.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(B2,$H$2:$J$6,3,FALSE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with B2 as lookup value. 1 mark: absolute range $H$2:$J$6. 1 mark: column 3 and FALSE (exact match). Accept 0 for FALSE; accept a named range.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B2 contains ISB. State the value displayed in C2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: B5 contains MUX. State what is displayed in C5 and explain why.
parts.answer: #N/A (an error); MUX is not in the first column of the lookup table and an exact match was requested.
parts.working: 1 mark: #N/A / error. 1 mark: reason.

practice.stem:
A wholesaler gives a discount based on the order value. The table in F2:G5 is:
F (order value from, Rs) | G (discount)
0 | 0%
5000 | 5%
10000 | 8%
20000 | 12%

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to find the discount rate for the order value in B2, using the table, so that it works when replicated.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(B2,$F$2:$G$5,2,TRUE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with B2 and absolute $F$2:$G$5. 1 mark: column 2 with TRUE (approximate match); accept TRUE omitted.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the discount rate given for order values of Rs 4999, Rs 10 000, Rs 17 500 and Rs 25 000.
parts.working: 2 marks all four; 1 mark for two or three.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the discount, in rupees, on an order of Rs 17 500.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why the values in column F must be in ascending order.
parts.answer: An approximate-match lookup searches for the largest value that is less than or equal to the lookup value, which only works correctly if the first column is sorted in ascending order.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A pharmacy stock sheet has product codes in A2:A9, product names in B2:B9, prices in C2:C9 and stock levels in D2:D9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in H3 using XLOOKUP that displays the stock level for the product code typed in H2. If the code is not found, the cell must display Not found.
parts.answer: =XLOOKUP(H2,A2:A9,D2:D9,"Not found")
parts.working: 1 mark: XLOOKUP with H2 as lookup value. 1 mark: lookup array A2:A9 and return array D2:D9. 1 mark: "Not found" as the if-not-found argument.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one advantage of XLOOKUP compared with VLOOKUP.
parts.answer: e.g. the return column can be to the left of the lookup column; it does not break if columns are inserted (no column number); exact match is the default; it has a built-in 'not found' value.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A mixed-reference times table: B1:D1 contain 5, 6, 7 and A2:A4 contain 2, 3, 4. B2 contains =$A2*B$1 and is replicated to fill B2:D4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in D4 after replication.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the values displayed in C3 and D4.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the formula would give wrong answers if it had been entered as =A2*B1 before being replicated.
parts.answer: Both references would change in both directions, e.g. in D4 it would become =C4*D3, which multiplies results instead of the row and column headings; the $ before A keeps the column fixed and the $ before 1 keeps the row fixed.
parts.working: 1 mark: relative references move in both directions / point to wrong cells. 1 mark: explanation of what $A and $1 lock.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula for F2 to calculate the delivery charge. Delivery is free if the order total in D2 is more than Rs 5000. Otherwise it is Rs 500 if E2 contains Express and Rs 250 for any other delivery type.
parts.working: 1 mark: IF(D2>5000,0,… ). 1 mark: nested IF testing E2="Express". 1 mark: 500 and 250 in the correct positions. 1 mark: correct syntax/brackets.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the charge for: (i) D2 = 6200, E2 = Express (ii) D2 = 3100, E2 = Express (iii) D2 = 5000, E2 = Standard.
parts.working: 1 mark each. (iii): 5000 is not more than 5000.

practice.stem: A family in Rawalpindi records monthly electricity bills (Rs) in B2:B13 for January to December. The bills for November and December have not arrived, so B12 and B13 are empty. B2:B11 contain 8450, 7920, 9310, 11240, 13680, 15020, 14760, 12890, 10330, 9050.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value displayed by =AVERAGE(B2:B13).
parts.working: B1: 112 650 ÷ 10 = 11 265 (blank cells ignored).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed by =SUM(B2:B13)/12.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the two results are different and state which one gives the correct mean bill so far.
parts.answer: AVERAGE ignores the two empty cells and divides by 10 (the number of bills); SUM/12 divides by 12 including the months with no bill. AVERAGE gives the correct mean of the bills received.
parts.working: 1 mark: AVERAGE ignores blanks / divides by 10. 1 mark: AVERAGE is correct.

practice.stem: A student's bank transactions (Rs) are in B2:B9. Deposits are positive and withdrawals negative: 5000, −1200, −350, 2500, −800, 1500, −2000, 700.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a function to calculate the total of all the withdrawals (negative values) and state its value.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula using SUMIF and COUNTIF to calculate the mean deposit (positive values) and state its value.
parts.working: 1 mark formula; B1: 9700 ÷ 4 = 2425.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write a single function that gives the same result as the formula in (b).
parts.answer: =AVERAGEIF(B2:B9,">0")
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A garden centre's sheet has a named range Prices covering a table: column 1 product code, column 2 product name, column 3 unit price (Rs). The discount rate for loyal customers is in cell H1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to calculate the cost of the order: look up the unit price of the product code in A2 from the Prices range, multiply by the quantity in B2 and apply the discount in H1. It must work when replicated.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices,3,FALSE)*B2*(1-$H$1)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP(A2,Prices,…). 1 mark: column 3, FALSE. 1 mark: ×B2. 1 mark: ×(1−$H$1) with absolute reference. Accept equivalent e.g. −…*$H$1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A2 contains F07, whose unit price is Rs 1240. B2 contains 3 and H1 contains 10%. State the value displayed in C2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher wants C2 to show Pass when the mark in B2 is 50 or more. She has entered =IF(B2>50,"Pass","Fail"). Give a test value for B2 that would show the formula is wrong, and state the output it gives and the output expected.
parts.answer: 50; it displays Fail but Pass is expected.
parts.working: 1 mark: 50 (the boundary). 1 mark: Fail given, Pass expected.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the corrected formula.
parts.answer: =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")
parts.working: 1 mark. Accept =IF(B2<50,"Fail","Pass").

parts.label: c
parts.text: Marks are whole numbers from 0 to 100. Give two further test values, other than your answer to (a), that test the corrected formula on each side of the boundary, with the expected output for each.
parts.answer: 49 → Fail; 51 → Pass (accept e.g. 0 → Fail, 100 → Pass with explanation as extreme data).
parts.working: 1 mark each: value with correct expected output.

practice.stem: Column A holds the salary (Rs), column B the performance rating and column C the number of years of service.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D2 that calculates the bonus: 10% of the salary in A2 if the years in C2 are 5 or more AND the rating in B2 is A; 5% if only one of these conditions is true; otherwise 0.
parts.working: 1 mark: outer IF on AND (both conditions) giving 10%. 1 mark: inner IF on OR for 5%. 1 mark: the final 0 for neither. 1 mark: correct percentages applied to the salary in A2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the bonus for these rows (salary, rating, years): (40000, A, 6); (30000, A, 2); (50000, B, 7); (25000, B, 1).
parts.working: 1 mark for the first two (4000 and 1500). 1 mark for the last two (2500 and 0).

practice.stem: An online shop charges delivery by weight (in kg in cell B2). The price of the item (Rs) is in cell A2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula that calculates the total charge for the delivery: price in A2 plus a delivery charge in B2 of Rs 0 for weight up to 1 kg, Rs 150 for weight over 1 kg up to 5 kg, and Rs 300 for weight over 5 kg.
parts.working: 1 mark: the price is added. 1 mark: nested IF for the 1 kg boundary. 1 mark: the 5 kg boundary gives Rs 300.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the total charge for a price of 2000 and a weight of 3.5 kg, and for a price of 1000 and a weight of 6 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in G2 that calculates the mean of only the positive values in B2:B30, without using an array formula.
parts.answer: =SUMIF(B2:B30,">0")/COUNTIF(B2:B30,">0")
parts.working: 1 mark: SUMIF of positive values. 1 mark: COUNTIF of positive values as the divisor. 1 mark: the division with correct criteria in quotes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the formula =AVERAGE(B2:B30) gives a different answer from the formula in part a.
parts.answer: AVERAGE includes the zero and negative values, so the mean is lower (or includes those values in the total and count).
parts.working: 1 mark: AVERAGE includes all the numbers. 1 mark: this changes the mean when zero or negative values are present.

practice.stem: A stock sheet has the stock level in B2, the reorder level in E2 and a discontinued flag (Yes or No) in D2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in F2 that displays Order now if the stock in B2 is less than the reorder level in E2 and the item is not discontinued (column D is not Yes); Check if the item is discontinued; OK otherwise.
parts.answer: =IF(D2="Yes","Check",IF(B2<E2,"Order now","OK"))
parts.working: 1 mark: the discontinued test is first. 1 mark: the stock less than reorder level test. 1 mark: the correct three outputs in quotes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the output in F2 for these rows (stock, reorder level, discontinued): (12, 20, No); (35, 20, No); (5, 20, Yes).
parts.answer: Order now; OK; Check
parts.working: 1 mark for the first two rows. 1 mark for the third row.

practice.stem: A school uses a grade table in F2 to G7, in which the marks in F2 to F7 are in ascending order.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in B2 that displays the grade for the score in A2 using the table in F2:G7, with approximate matching. F holds the lowest mark for each grade (0, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80) and G holds the grade (U, E, D, C, B, A).
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(A2,F2:G7,2,TRUE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with lookup value A2. 1 mark: the table F2:G7 and column index 2. 1 mark: TRUE for approximate match (sorted lowest mark first).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the grade displayed for scores 39, 50 and 79.
parts.answer: U; D; B
parts.working: 1 mark for 39 (U) and 50 (D). 1 mark for 79 (B).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in D2 that calculates the price after the 20% discount: the discount applies only if the age in C2 is under 18 OR the card in D2 is Yes. Use the price in B2.
parts.working: 1 mark: IF with OR for the two conditions. 1 mark: multiplying by 0.8 (20% off). 1 mark: the else value B2 with no discount.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the price shown for a price of 300 for a student aged 16 without a card, and for a price of 300 for an adult aged 30 without a card.
parts.working: 1 mark for 240 (300 × 0.8). 1 mark for 300 (no discount).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in E2 that calculates 15% of the total of the amounts in column B for only those rows where column C is marked Yes.
parts.working: 1 mark: SUMIF over the amounts in B2:B40. 1 mark: criteria range C2:C40 and "Yes". 1 mark: multiply the total by 0.15. The formula is in E2, outside the criteria range, so it is not circular.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the tax when the Yes amounts are 1000 and 2500 and the No amount is 800.
parts.answer: Rs 525
parts.working: 1 mark for the total of taxable items 3500. 1 mark for 3500 × 0.15 = 525.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 that calculates the value one year later, if the value in B2 grows by 4% per year.
parts.working: 1 mark: multiplies B2 by 1.04.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B2 holds 10 000. Calculate the value after three years of 4% growth, to 2 decimal places. Show the value after each year.
parts.working: 1 mark for year 1 (10 400). 1 mark for year 2 (10 816). 1 mark for year 3 (11 248.64, rounded to 2 decimal places).

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the values displayed by =ROUND(B2,0) and by =INT(B2) when B2 contains −3.4.
parts.answer: ROUND gives −3; INT gives −4
parts.working: 1 mark for ROUND gives −3 (−3.4 rounds to −3). 1 mark for INT gives −4 (INT returns the next lower whole number).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between ROUND and INT for negative numbers.
parts.answer: ROUND rounds to the nearest whole number; INT always rounds down to the next lower whole number, so −3.4 becomes −4.
parts.working: 1 mark: ROUND goes to the nearest. 1 mark: INT always goes down (towards negative infinity).

practice.stem: Cells B2 to B31 hold the daily maximum temperature (°C) for a month. Cell B33 holds the threshold 35.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in B34 that counts how many days in B2:B31 have a temperature of at least the threshold in B33.
parts.answer: =COUNTIF(B2:B31,">="&B33)
parts.working: 1 mark: COUNTIF on B2:B31. 1 mark: the criterion ">=" joined to B33 with &.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed in B34 if B33 contains 35 and the only values in B2 to B31 that are 35 or more are 35, 36 and 35.
parts.working: 1 mark: three values (35, 36, 35) meet the threshold.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write down the most suitable generic file extension for each file.
(i) Plain text with no formatting, such as a list of names.
(ii) A table of data with the values separated by commas.
(iii) A formatted letter that can be opened and edited in most word processors.
(iv) A leaflet whose layout must look exactly the same on every computer and printer.
parts.answer:
(i) .txt
(ii) .csv
(iii) .rtf
(iv) .pdf
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write the full name of each file format.
(i) .css
(ii) .pdf
(iii) .rtf
(iv) .csv
parts.answer:
(i) Cascading Style Sheet(s)
(ii) Portable Document Format
(iii) Rich Text Format
(iv) Comma Separated Values
parts.working: 1 mark each; spelling must be recognisable.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a .zip file.
parts.answer: A compressed file (archive) that can contain one or more files/folders in a smaller size (lossless).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two reasons for zipping a folder of files before emailing it.
parts.answer: Any two, e.g. smaller file is quicker to upload/download; may fit within the email attachment size limit; many files are sent as one attachment; uses less storage space; can be password protected.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem:
A file called MARKS.csv contains lines such as:
Ali Raza,Lahore,85
Sara Khan,Karachi,92

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what the commas in the file do.
parts.answer: They separate the values/fields in each record (each comma marks the end of one field).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name two types of software that can open this file.
parts.answer: Any two of: spreadsheet; database; text editor; word processor.
parts.working: 1 mark for two.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write down the most suitable file format for each file.
(i) A photograph of Badshahi Mosque on a website.
(ii) A school logo that must have a transparent background.
(iii) A short looping animated banner with a few colours.
(iv) A podcast episode for download.
(v) A video clip of a cricket match.
parts.answer:
(i) .jpg
(ii) .png (accept .gif)
(iii) .gif
(iv) .mp3
(v) .mp4
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a file name has an extension such as .docx or .png.
parts.answer: The extension tells the operating system what type of file it is and therefore which software to use to open it; it also lets the user see the file type.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State whether each file normally stores an image, audio, video or text.
(i) .png
(ii) .mp3
(iii) .mp4
(iv) .txt
(v) .gif
(vi) .csv
parts.answer:
(i) Image
(ii) Audio
(iii) Video
(iv) Text
(v) Image
(vi) Text (data)
parts.working: All six: 3 marks; four or five: 2 marks; two or three: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: You are given these files: banner.jpg, notes.txt, style4.css, map.png, logo.jpg, prices.csv. You are told to copy only the image files with a .jpg extension and the stylesheet into a new folder. List the files you copy.
parts.answer: banner.jpg, logo.jpg, style4.css
parts.working: 1 mark for both .jpg files only, 1 mark for style4.css; lose 1 mark for each extra file.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why web page file names should not contain spaces.
parts.answer: Spaces can cause broken links on some web servers/browsers (they become %20 in the URL); file names must match exactly.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A college in Hyderabad publishes its examination timetable as a .pdf file on its website. Give two advantages of using .pdf.
parts.answer: Any two, e.g. students can open it on any device without the original software; layout looks the same on every device/printer; students cannot easily change the times; small file size quick to download.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write down the most suitable file format for each purpose.
(i) An application form attached to an email that must look the same for everyone and should not be edited.
(ii) Data moved from one database package to a different database package.
(iii) A file holding the colours and fonts used by every page of a website.
parts.answer:
(i) .pdf
(ii) .csv
(iii) .css
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what kind of image an .svg file stores.
parts.answer: A vector image, described by shapes and mathematical lines rather than a grid of pixels.
parts.working: 1 mark: vector graphics / shapes described mathematically.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one advantage of this for a school logo that is printed in many different sizes.
parts.answer: It can be enlarged or reduced without losing quality or becoming blocky.
parts.working: 1 mark: no loss of quality when resized.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name a common image file format that stores pixel data without compression.
parts.answer: BMP (bitmap)
parts.working: 1 mark: BMP.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what an .exe file is.
parts.answer: An executable file: a program that runs when it is opened.
parts.working: 1 mark: an executable program.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why an .exe file attached to an unexpected email should not be opened.
parts.answer: It may be malware that is run as soon as the file is opened.
parts.working: 1 mark: may contain malware that runs when opened.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State which software creates a .pptx file.
parts.answer: Microsoft PowerPoint
parts.working: 1 mark: Microsoft PowerPoint.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name one other program that can open a .pptx file.
parts.answer: Any one: Google Slides; LibreOffice Impress; WPS Office; a PowerPoint viewer.
parts.working: 1 mark: any valid program.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name a lossless audio format.
parts.answer: WAV or FLAC.
parts.working: 1 mark: WAV or FLAC.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name a lossy audio format.
parts.answer: MP3 or AAC.
parts.working: 1 mark: MP3 or AAC.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name two file formats that support transparent backgrounds for images on a web page.
parts.answer: PNG and GIF.
parts.working: 1 mark for each, up to 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State whether .jpg and .jpeg are different file formats.
parts.answer: No, they are the same format with two different extensions.
parts.working: 1 mark: same format.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the reason that the .jpg extension is often used.
parts.answer: It is a shortened form of the extension, with three letters, which older systems required.
parts.working: 1 mark: three-letter extension for older systems (any valid reason).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the software that normally creates each spreadsheet file: (i) .xlsx (ii) .ods (iii) .xls
parts.answer: (i) Microsoft Excel (ii) LibreOffice Calc (OpenDocument spreadsheet) (iii) Microsoft Excel (older version, pre-2007 format)
parts.working: 1 mark for each correct software; (iii) may also be described as the older Excel binary format.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a compressed file.
parts.answer: A file whose data has been encoded so it takes less storage space and is quicker to send.
parts.working: 1 mark: data encoded to take less space. 1 mark: smaller to store or transfer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give one reason why a photographer might keep the master copy of a picture as a .tiff file.
parts.answer: It is a high-quality, lossless format that keeps all the image detail for later editing and printing.
parts.working: 1 mark: lossless / high quality / suitable for editing and printing.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why generic file formats are needed when files are shared between people.
parts.answer: Different people use different software/operating systems; a generic format can be opened by many different applications on any platform, so the receiver does not need the same software as the sender.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give an example of a situation where a generic file format would be used.
parts.answer: E.g. a school sending a timetable as .pdf to all parents; a company exporting sales data as .csv to import into a different database; sending a report as .rtf to someone with different word-processing software.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A web designer in Islamabad is choosing between .jpg and .png files for the images on a travel website. Compare the two formats.
parts.answer: Both are compressed image formats supported by all web browsers. JPG uses lossy compression so files are smaller and load faster, while PNG uses lossless compression so no detail is lost but files are larger; JPG suits photographs with many colours, PNG suits logos/text/diagrams with sharp edges; PNG supports transparent backgrounds whereas JPG does not; repeatedly editing and saving a JPG lowers its quality.
parts.working: 1 mark per comparison point, max 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two uses of .gif files on websites.
parts.answer: Any two, e.g. short simple animations/animated banners; small icons/buttons; simple graphics with few colours; images with a transparent background.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why .gif is not suitable for a detailed colour photograph.
parts.answer: GIF can only store a limited palette of 256 colours, so photos with many shades would lose quality.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State what type of data is stored in each format.
(i) .mp3
(ii) .mp4
parts.answer:
(i) Audio/sound (music)
(ii) Video (with sound) – multimedia
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how an .mp3 file is made much smaller than the original recording.
parts.answer: Lossy compression removes sounds that humans cannot hear or are unlikely to notice (e.g. very high/low frequencies, quieter sounds masked by louder ones).
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: In a practical task you are given a file called NEWSLETTER.rtf to edit.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why you should save the file in your word processor's own format before you start editing.
parts.answer: The software's own format keeps all the features you add (styles, headers/footers with automated fields, section breaks, wrapped images); some of these may be lost or changed if the document is saved as .rtf.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The finished newsletter is to be sent to a printing company as a .pdf file. Give two reasons why .pdf is used.
parts.answer: Any two, e.g. layout, fonts and images appear exactly as designed on any computer/printer; the printer does not need the same word processor; the file cannot be easily edited by mistake; the file is compact; fonts can be embedded.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A website uses an external stylesheet. State what is stored in the .css file and what is stored in the .htm file.
parts.answer: .css: the styles/presentation rules (fonts, colours, sizes, alignment) for elements; .htm: the content and structure of the page (text, tables, images, links) in HTML.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the HTML element, placed in the head section, that attaches a stylesheet called style1.css stored in the same folder as the web page.
parts.answer: <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="style1.css">
parts.working: 1 mark: rel="stylesheet" and href="style1.css" required; type attribute optional; filename case must match.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare .txt and .rtf files.
parts.answer: Both are generic text formats that can be opened by most word processors/text editors. A .txt file stores only the characters with no formatting, whereas .rtf keeps formatting such as fonts, bold, colours and alignment; .txt files are smaller; .rtf can include tables/images while .txt cannot; .txt is used for simple notes/data/code, .rtf for formatted documents shared between different word processors.
parts.working: 1 mark per comparison point, max 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a database task you are given data in .csv files to import. Explain why the data is supplied in .csv format.
parts.answer: CSV is a generic, plain-text format; it can be imported into any database software, whichever package the candidate uses.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When importing a .csv file, the first row contains the field names. State the setting you choose during import so that these become field names and not a record.
parts.answer: Select 'First row contains field names/headings'.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is stored in an .htm file and name one type of software that can open it.
parts.answer: The HTML code (tags and content) of a web page; opened by a web browser (or a text editor/web-authoring software).
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A web page refers to its images using relative file paths such as . Explain why the image files must be copied into the same folder when the website is moved to a new computer.
parts.answer: A relative path tells the browser to look for the file in the same folder as the page; if the image is not there it cannot be found and will not display.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher opens the file SCORES.csv in a text editor and then in a spreadsheet. Describe what she sees in each case.
parts.answer: Text editor: plain lines of text with the values separated by commas (one record per line). Spreadsheet: each value placed in its own cell, in rows and columns.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: She had typed a formula to total the scores before saving as .csv. Explain what happens to the formula.
parts.answer: Only the result/value is saved; the formula itself is lost.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher sends a spreadsheet to a colleague who has an older version of the spreadsheet software. Explain why the teacher might save it as an older format such as .xls or as .csv.
parts.answer: The older program may not be able to open a newer .xlsx file, so an older format that the colleague's software can read is used; .csv keeps the values but loses formulas and formatting.
parts.working: 1 mark: the older software cannot open the newer format so an older format is used. 1 mark: .csv or .xls can be read by the colleague's software (with the loss of formatting or formulas noted).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between a raster image and a vector image. Give one file format for each.
parts.answer: A raster image is a grid of pixels, so it becomes blocky when enlarged (e.g. .jpg or .png); a vector image is made of shapes described by mathematics, so it can be scaled without loss of quality (e.g. .svg).
parts.working: 1 mark: raster as a grid of pixels that loses quality when enlarged. 1 mark: vector as shapes described mathematically. 1 mark: a correct format for each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a .bmp file of a photograph is much larger than a .jpg file of the same photograph.
parts.answer: The .bmp file stores the colour of every pixel without compression; the .jpg uses lossy compression that removes detail the eye is unlikely to notice.
parts.working: 1 mark: bmp uncompressed, every pixel stored. 1 mark: jpg compresses by removing detail.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe two ways to share a slideshow so that the viewer cannot change the slides.
parts.answer: Any two: save or export the presentation as a PDF; save it as a PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) that opens straight into slideshow mode; mark it as final or share it as read-only.
parts.working: 1 mark for each valid method, up to 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why an .mp4 file can contain both sound and pictures.
parts.answer: .mp4 is a container format that stores a compressed video stream and an audio stream together in one file.
parts.working: 1 mark: a container holding video and audio. 1 mark: each stream is compressed and stored together.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a password-protected zip file is useful when sending personal data by email.
parts.answer: The contents are encrypted, so anyone who intercepts the email cannot read the data without the password.
parts.working: 1 mark: contents encrypted. 1 mark: data remains unreadable if the email is intercepted, unless the password is known.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An email attachment is named invoice.pdf.exe. Explain why this file is dangerous.
parts.answer: Windows may hide the real .exe extension, so the file appears to be a PDF; .exe is an executable program, which may install malware when opened.
parts.working: 1 mark: the extension is hidden or disguised as a pdf. 1 mark: an executable program that can install malware when opened.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State what the recipient should do with this email.
parts.answer: Do not open the attachment; delete the email and report it to the sender's company or the IT department.
parts.working: 1 mark: do not open; delete or report.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A photo editing app saves a photograph as a .gif with 256 colours. Explain the effect on the image.
parts.answer: The number of colours is reduced, so smooth gradients show visible bands or blocks of colour and the photograph looks less realistic.
parts.working: 1 mark: fewer colours available. 1 mark: banding or loss of smooth colour transitions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a web designer should not place a 4 MB photograph on a web page without reducing its size.
parts.answer: The page takes a long time to load on a slow connection, which uses more bandwidth and frustrates visitors.
parts.working: 1 mark: slow loading or large download. 1 mark: uses bandwidth and annoys visitors; the file should be resized or compressed first.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the same .docx document may look different when opened in two different word-processing programs.
parts.answer: The program may not have the same fonts installed, and different programs can position text and images in slightly different ways.
parts.working: 1 mark: fonts or features missing or substituted. 1 mark: different software displays the layout differently.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression.
parts.answer: Lossy compression permanently removes some data (detail that is least noticeable), so the original cannot be restored exactly; lossless compression reduces the file size without losing any data, so the original can be rebuilt exactly.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
State which type of compression should be used for each file and give a reason.
(i) A spreadsheet of bank account balances.
(ii) A song to be streamed to mobile phones.
parts.answer:
(i) Lossless – every digit must be kept exactly/losing data would change the balances.
(ii) Lossy (e.g. .mp3) – much smaller file so it streams quickly using less data; the lost sounds are hard for people to hear.
parts.working: (i) 1 mark for lossless with reason; (ii) 1 mark for lossy, 1 mark for reason.

practice.stem: A recording of a qawwali performance is stored as a 40 MB uncompressed audio file. Converting it to .mp3 reduces the file size by 85%. Use 1 GB = 1024 MB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the size of the .mp3 file in MB.
parts.answer: 6 MB

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate how many whole .mp3 files of this size can be stored in 2 GB.
parts.answer: 341 files

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one drawback of using .mp3 for this recording.
parts.answer: Some sound quality is lost permanently and cannot be recovered (lossy).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student types CSS rules in a word processor and saves the file as house.rtf. He renames it house.css and attaches it to his web page, but none of the styles appear. Explain why.
parts.answer: The .rtf file contains formatting codes/control words as well as the CSS text; renaming does not remove them, so the browser cannot read the rules (invalid CSS).
parts.working: 1 mark for formatting codes in rtf, 1 mark for browser cannot interpret them.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how he should create the stylesheet so that it works.
parts.answer: Type the rules in a text editor (or the web-authoring software) and save as plain text with the .css extension.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A school in Rawalpindi plans to email its 20-page prospectus to parents as a .pdf file instead of a word-processed file. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using .pdf.
parts.answer: Advantages: parents can open it on any device with a free reader/web browser; layout, fonts and images look exactly as designed; parents cannot easily change the content; can be compressed to a smaller file for emailing; can include links/bookmarks; can be printed accurately. Disadvantages: hard for the school or parents to edit/update – a new PDF must be made from the original; large if it contains many high-quality images; text may be hard to read on small phone screens because it does not reflow; screen readers may not read it well if not tagged; fill-in sections need special software. Conclusion.
parts.working: 5–6: both sides developed and linked to the prospectus, with conclusion; 3–4: both sides with some development; 1–2: simple points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A shop manager saves her sales spreadsheet in .csv format so that it can be imported into an accounts system. Describe three things that will be lost when the spreadsheet is saved as .csv.
parts.answer: Any three, e.g. formulas – only the calculated values are saved; cell formatting such as fonts, colours, borders, currency symbols; charts and images; additional worksheets – only the active sheet is saved; column widths/merged cells; named ranges/conditional formatting.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why .csv is still a good choice for transferring the data.
parts.answer: It is plain text that almost any spreadsheet/database/accounts software can import, whatever software created it.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A school photographer has a photo of a science fair stored as a 2.88 MB file. After saving it as a .jpg the file is 0.36 MB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage reduction in file size.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the photographer should keep a copy of the original file as well as the .jpg.
parts.answer: JPG compression is lossy, so detail removed cannot be recovered; the original is needed for high-quality printing/later editing, and re-saving a JPG reduces quality further.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem: Imran wants to email 25 holiday photos from Swat to his cousin in Toronto. The photos are .jpg files with a total size of 180 MB. His email service allows attachments of up to 25 MB per email.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the smallest number of emails needed if the photos are sent without changing them.
parts.answer: 8 emails
parts.working: 180 ÷ 25 = 7.2, so round up to 8 emails.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Imran zips the photos but the zip file is still about 175 MB. Explain why.
parts.answer: JPG files are already compressed (lossy), so lossless zip compression can make them only slightly smaller.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe two other ways Imran could send the photos.
parts.answer: Reduce the resolution/quality of the photos (lossy) so they fit in fewer emails; upload them to cloud storage and email a link with shared access; use a file-transfer service.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A video-streaming service stores films as compressed .mp4 files. Describe how lossy compression reduces the size of a video file.
parts.answer: Removes detail that viewers are unlikely to notice (e.g. small colour differences); stores only the parts of each frame that change from the previous frame instead of every whole frame; reduces the resolution/frame rate/bit rate; removes inaudible sounds from the soundtrack.
parts.working: 1 mark per point, max 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain one reason why the service uses lossy rather than lossless compression.
parts.answer: Lossy compression gives much smaller files, so films stream without buffering and use less data/storage; the small loss of quality is hardly noticed.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A photographer in Hunza is sending landscape photos to a magazine that will print them on large pages. Discuss whether she should send the photos as highly compressed .jpg files or in a lossless format such as .png.
parts.answer: JPG (high compression): much smaller files, quick to upload over a slow mountain internet connection, fit email limits, use less storage; but lossy – fine detail and colour gradients (sky) may show blocks/artefacts when printed large, and quality cannot be recovered. Lossless (.png): keeps every pixel, best quality for large printing and further editing by the magazine; but files are much larger, slow to upload, may need cloud storage/file transfer. Middle way: JPG at high quality/low compression, or send small previews first then full files of chosen photos. Conclusion, e.g. lossless/high-quality files because print quality is the priority.
parts.working: 5–6: both formats discussed in context with justified conclusion; 3–4: both sides with some development; 1–2: simple points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A web page must show the video clip tour.mp4 with controls that the user can use to play and pause it. If the browser cannot play the video, the text 'Video not supported' must be shown. Write the HTML to do this.
parts.answer:
<video controls>
  <source src="tour.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  Video not supported
</video>
parts.working: 1 mark for <video controls> … </video>; 1 mark for source with src="tour.mp4" (type="video/mp4"); 1 mark for fallback text placed inside the video element. Accept <video src="tour.mp4" controls>Video not supported</video>.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why .mp4 is a suitable format for video on a web page.
parts.answer: It is supported by almost all browsers/devices and is compressed so it downloads/streams quickly.
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem: A 1920 × 1080 pixel image is saved as an uncompressed .bmp file. Each pixel uses 24 bits.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the size of the uncompressed image in bytes.
parts.answer: 6 220 800 bytes

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the size of the image in MB, correct to 2 decimal places. Use 1 MB = 1 000 000 bytes.

practice.stem: A 30-second stereo sound recording is saved as an uncompressed .wav file. It has a sampling rate of 44 100 samples per second and each sample uses 16 bits.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the size of the recording in MB, correct to 2 decimal places. Use 1 MB = 1 000 000 bytes. Show your working.
parts.working: M1: 44 100 samples per second × 2 bytes (16 bits) = 88 200 bytes per second per channel. M1: × 2 channels × 30 seconds = 5 292 000 bytes. A1: 5.29 MB.

practice.stem: A 16 GB USB stick is used to store photographs. Each .jpg photograph is 2.8 MB. Use 1 GB = 1000 MB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate how many complete .jpg files of this size fit on the stick. Show your working.
parts.answer: 5714 files

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why the calculation gives a lower number than the stick can hold in practice.
parts.answer: The stick also stores the file system and other files, so less space is available.
parts.working: 1 mark: any valid reason, e.g. file system overhead or other files on the stick.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Discuss which file format is most suitable for a student's final project saved in .docx, .pdf or .rtf, considering compatibility, editing and size.
parts.answer: A reasoned answer should discuss: .pdf keeps the layout exactly and opens everywhere, but cannot be edited easily; .docx allows editing and keeps formatting, but needs compatible software; .rtf opens in many programs and keeps basic formatting but has no advanced features. The best choice is judged by the purpose, for example a .pdf for submission and the .docx kept for editing.
parts.working: Mark bands: 5–6 marks for a discussion of all three formats against compatibility, editing and size with a reasoned choice. 3–4 marks for two formats discussed with reasons. 1–2 marks for a general statement.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why lossy compression is unsuitable for a medical scan image but suitable for a streamed video.
parts.answer: A medical scan needs every detail to be accurate for diagnosis, and lossy compression permanently removes detail; a streamed video can lose some detail the viewer will not notice, which saves bandwidth.
parts.working: 1 mark: lossy removes data permanently. 1 mark: scan detail matters for diagnosis. 1 mark: the viewer does not notice the lost detail in video and streaming saves bandwidth.

practice.stem: A 10-minute video clip is encoded at a steady 2.5 Mbit/s (megabits per second). 1 byte = 8 bits.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the total number of megabits needed to stream the clip. Show your working.
parts.answer: 1500 Mbit

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the size of the clip in MB.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate the file formats (.png, .jpg and .svg) that are most suitable for a company logo used on a website, on a banner printed 3 metres wide and as a small favicon.
parts.answer: A reasoned evaluation should note that .svg is ideal for the logo because it can be scaled to any size without losing quality and is small; .png suits the favicon and the logo on a website if the vector file is not available, as it keeps sharp edges and transparency; .jpg is unsuitable for the logo because it has no transparency and blurs edges; the 3 m banner needs a vector format or a very high resolution image.
parts.working: Mark bands: 5–6 marks for a justified choice for all three uses, with at least two formats evaluated against scaling, transparency and file size. 3–4 marks for a choice for two uses with reasons. 1–2 marks for a generic list.

practice.stem: A student saves a list of student numbers such as 00123 and 00456 in a .csv file. When she opens the file in a spreadsheet, the first zeros have disappeared.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the leading zeros disappear when the file is opened in a spreadsheet.
parts.answer: The spreadsheet treats numbers such as 00123 as numeric values, so the leading zeros carry no value and are removed.
parts.working: 1 mark: spreadsheet reads the entries as numbers. 1 mark: leading zeros are dropped because numbers do not store them.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how to keep the leading zeros when the file is opened.
parts.answer: Format the column as text before the data is entered, or import the file and choose the column type Text.
parts.working: 1 mark: set column as Text on import or formatting.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain how converting a .wav file to .mp3 reduces the file size and changes the quality.
parts.answer: MP3 uses lossy compression, which removes sound that the ear is less likely to notice, so the file is smaller but the quality is reduced.
parts.working: 1 mark: lossy compression removes data to reduce size. 1 mark: quality is reduced.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the original .wav file should be kept.
parts.answer: Converting the file again would lose more quality, and the original is needed for further editing.
parts.working: 1 mark: further conversions reduce quality, so the original is kept for editing.

practice.stem: A folder of holiday photographs and documents is compressed into a single zip file. The four files total 18.6 MB before compression and 7.4 MB after compression.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the compression ratio of the zip file, correct to 2 decimal places, as a ratio of original size to compressed size.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a zip file containing already-compressed .jpg files would not shrink much.
parts.answer: The jpg data is already compressed, so zip cannot remove much more redundancy.
parts.working: 1 mark: data already compressed.

practice.stem: A student is preparing a leaflet about a tree-planting drive in Islamabad. The heading is in a serif font and the body text is in a sans-serif font.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the difference between a serif font and a sans-serif font.
parts.answer: A serif font has small extra strokes (tails/feet) at the ends of the letter strokes; a sans-serif font has no such strokes, so the letter ends are plain.
parts.working: B1 serif has small lines/strokes/tails at the ends of characters. B1 sans-serif has none (plain ends). Do not credit naming fonts only.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why a sans-serif font is often chosen for text read on a screen or from a distance.
parts.answer: Its plain letter shapes are clearer/easier to read on a screen or at a distance (e.g. on a poster).
parts.working: B1 clearer / more legible on screen or from far away. Not just 'looks better'.

practice.stem:
A house style for a company newsletter says:
• page size A4, orientation portrait
• all margins 2 cm
• body text: sans-serif font, 11 point, fully justified
• line spacing: single, with 6 points of space after each paragraph

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the setting you would change so that the text lines up with both the left and the right margins.
parts.answer: Alignment set to fully justified (justify).
parts.working: B1 justify / fully justified alignment.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between line spacing and paragraph spacing.
parts.answer: Line spacing is the vertical gap between the lines of text inside a paragraph; paragraph spacing is extra space added before or after a whole paragraph (between one paragraph and the next).
parts.working: B1 line spacing = distance between lines within a paragraph. B1 paragraph spacing = space before/after a paragraph.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the setting that controls whether the long edge of the page is horizontal or vertical, and the value needed here.
parts.answer: Page orientation, set to portrait.
parts.working: B1 orientation – portrait (long edge vertical).

practice.stem: After editing a 6-page document, a student is asked to check that there are no widows or orphans.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a widow and an orphan in a word-processed document.
parts.answer: A widow is the last line of a paragraph left on its own at the top of a new page (or column); an orphan is the first line of a paragraph left on its own at the bottom of a page (or column).
parts.working: B1 widow: last line of paragraph alone at top of page/column. B1 orphan: first line alone at bottom of page/column. (Accept descriptions that also include a heading separated from its text at the bottom of a page for orphan-like errors only if clearly explained.)

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one way of removing a widow without changing the words of the document.
parts.answer: Turn on widow/orphan control (or insert a page break before the paragraph / keep lines together).
parts.working: B1 any one: widow and orphan control; keep lines together; insert page/column break before the paragraph; adjust spacing slightly.

practice.stem:
A school in Multan produces a prize-giving programme. Four items appear on the first page:
1 the main title
2 the body paragraphs
3 the date and venue in the top-right area
4 a list of prices in a table column

parts.label: a
parts.text: For each item, state the most suitable text alignment.
parts.answer: 1 centre; 2 fully justified (or left); 3 right aligned; 4 right aligned (or decimal-aligned) so that the digits line up.
parts.working: B1 each: title – centred; body – justified/left; date/venue – right; prices – right/decimal tab.

practice.stem: A recipe card for making chicken karahi lists the ingredients and then the steps of the method.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State whether a bulleted list or a numbered list is more suitable for the ingredients. Give a reason.
parts.answer: Bulleted list, because the order of the ingredients does not matter.
parts.working: B1 bulleted. B1 order not important / items are equal.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State whether a bulleted list or a numbered list is more suitable for the method. Give a reason.
parts.answer: Numbered list, because the steps must be followed in a set order and can be referred to by number.
parts.working: B1 numbered. B1 sequence matters / easy to refer to step number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sports club is printing a table with 14 columns of match results. State the page orientation that should be used and give a reason.
parts.answer: Landscape, because the page is wider so all 14 columns fit across without being too narrow or splitting the table.
parts.working: B1 landscape. B1 wider page / more columns fit.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one type of document for which portrait orientation is normally used.
parts.answer: A letter (or report, essay, CV).
parts.working: B1 any suitable: letter, report, CV, essay, memo.

practice.stem: A chemistry worksheet must show the formula of carbon dioxide as CO₂ and the expression 10³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the text formatting needed for the 2 in CO₂.
parts.answer: Subscript.
parts.working: B1 subscript.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the text formatting needed for the 3 in 10³.
parts.answer: Superscript.
parts.working: B1 superscript.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the difference between a page break and a column break.
parts.answer: A page break forces the text after it to start on the next page; a column break forces the text after it to start at the top of the next column (on the same page if there is one).
parts.working: B1 page break → next page. B1 column break → next column.

practice.stem: A task says: enter the title Clean Water For Thar exactly as shown, in a 24 point bold font, centre aligned.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify three different formatting settings named in the task.
parts.answer: Font size 24 point; bold (font style); centre alignment.
parts.working: 1 mark each: 24 pt size; bold; centred.

parts.label: b
