parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain one risk of using Replace All and how to reduce it.
parts.answer: It may change text that should not be changed, for example the name inside a quotation or a web address; review the changes afterwards (or use Find Next and replace one at a time / match case).
parts.working: 1 mark: unintended replacements. 1 mark: proofread / match case / whole words / check each one.

practice.stem: An international aid organisation has offices in Pakistan, Jordan and Kenya. Documents are written in English, Urdu and Arabic. Head office wants one corporate house style for all offices.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Discuss the issues the organisation should consider when designing a single house style for all three offices.
parts.answer: The chosen fonts must support Urdu and Arabic script as well as English, so a font family with matching scripts is needed; Urdu and Arabic are written right to left, so alignment, page layout and logo position rules must work in mirrored form; font sizes may need adjusting because some scripts appear smaller at the same point size; colours and images must be culturally acceptable in each country; templates and styles must be shared with every office and staff trained. Benefits: a consistent, recognisable brand worldwide. Conclusion: one house style with language-specific variations defined in it.
parts.working: Up to 5 marks for issues/benefits, 1 mark for reasoned conclusion. Points: fonts must support all scripts | right-to-left text affects alignment/layout/indents | logo placement in mirrored layouts | relative font sizes differ between scripts | cultural meaning of colours/images | templates must be distributed and kept up to date | training and checking in each office | benefit – global brand consistency.

practice.stem: A house style for exam revision booklets states: 'No widows or orphans; no blank pages; each section heading must be on the same page as the paragraph that follows it.'

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a widow and an orphan in a document.
parts.answer: A widow is the last line of a paragraph that appears on its own at the top of a new page (or column); an orphan is the first line of a paragraph left on its own at the bottom of a page (or column).
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how paragraph style settings can be used to meet all three parts of this house style rule.
parts.answer: Turn on widow/orphan control in the body text style so single lines are never left alone; turn on 'keep with next' in the heading styles so each heading moves to the page of the next paragraph; use page breaks only where required (or page break before in a style) and remove empty paragraphs so no blank pages are created.
parts.working: 1 mark: widow/orphan control. 1 mark: keep with next on headings. 1 mark: remove extra blank paragraphs/unneeded page breaks to avoid blank pages.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State how a student could check the whole booklet for these errors before printing.
parts.answer: Use print preview (multi-page view) and look at the top and bottom of every page.
parts.working: B1: print preview / proofread each page / show formatting marks to find empty paragraphs.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Discuss whether a strict corporate house style is appropriate for worksheets written by teachers in one school. Give points for and against.
parts.answer: For: consistent look for students and parents; logo and fonts show the school's identity; readability can be planned for all students. Against: teachers need flexibility for different subjects and layouts; strict rules take time to follow; a worksheet for maths may need diagrams and tables that the style does not cover; a small set of simple rules (fonts, logo, margins) may be better than a full style. Conclusion: a light house style with clear rules for logos and headings, but flexibility for the content.
parts.working: Up to 6 marks: 2 marks for clear points for a strict style, 2 marks for clear points against it with reasons, and 2 marks for a justified balanced conclusion that suggests a suitable level of control.

practice.stem: A house style for a magazine uses four columns, each 5.0 cm wide, with gaps of 0.6 cm between columns. The text width on an A4 page with 2 cm margins is 17 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the total width of the four columns and the gaps. State whether they fit within a text width of 17 cm.
parts.answer: 4 × 5.0 + 3 × 0.6 = 21.8 cm. This is wider than 17 cm, so the four columns do not fit.
parts.working: M1: four column widths 4 × 5.0 = 20.0 cm. M1: three gaps 3 × 0.6 = 1.8 cm, total 21.8 cm. A1: it does not fit within 17 cm; at most three such columns can fit.

practice.stem: A company's corporate red is red 200, green 16, blue 46.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Convert the colour to its six-digit hexadecimal code. Then give the hex code for the second colour: red 0, green 0, blue 255.

practice.stem: A4 paper is 29.7 cm high. The top margin is 2.5 cm and the bottom margin is 2.0 cm. Each line of body text takes up 0.5 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of complete lines of text that fit on the page, given that each line takes 0.5 cm.
parts.answer: 50 lines
parts.working: M1: height available 29.7 − 2.5 − 2.0 = 25.2 cm. M1: 25.2 ÷ 0.5 = 50.4. A1: 50 complete lines (the part-line is not used).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the change to the Body style updates the whole document, while changes made to each paragraph by hand do not.
parts.answer: The paragraphs are linked to a style, so changing the style changes every paragraph that uses it; manual formatting is stored only in the paragraph it is applied to, so it does not change with the style.
parts.working: 1 mark: paragraphs use the style. 1 mark: changing the style changes all linked paragraphs. 1 mark: manual changes stay on individual paragraphs.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two situations where direct (manual) formatting is needed even when a house style exists.
parts.answer: Any two: a one-off special effect for a single paragraph; a single word in a different colour for emphasis; a special layout for a single page or table that the style does not cover.
parts.working: 1 mark for each valid situation.

practice.stem: A house style reduces the body text in a report from 12 pt to 10.5 pt.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage reduction in font size.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain how a designer should set this change so that all body text in the document changes at once.
parts.answer: Change the Body style to 10.5 pt and update it, so every paragraph using the Body style changes.
parts.working: 1 mark: change the style, not each paragraph. 1 mark: update the style so the document follows it.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how to make the appendix heading always start on a new page, using a paragraph style setting.
parts.answer: Open the paragraph settings for the Appendix heading style; in Line and Page Breaks tick Page break before; apply and update the style.
parts.working: 1 mark: open the style's paragraph settings. 1 mark: tick Page break before. 1 mark: apply or update the style so every appendix heading uses it.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain how a style based on another style lets a designer change a house style quickly, and state one risk of this method.
parts.answer: The designer changes one parent style (e.g. Body) and all styles based on it update automatically, so the whole document changes at once; risk: a change to the parent style can unexpectedly alter other styles or sections that were based on it, so the designer must check the whole document.
parts.working: 1 mark: styles based on another style inherit changes. 1 mark: one change updates many styles. 1 mark: a valid risk (unexpected changes to linked styles). 1 mark: the designer should check the result.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain how a house style can be made to work for a company with offices in Pakistan and in an English-speaking country, given that documents may be printed on different paper sizes.
parts.answer: Use A4 paper for both, or set the paper size in the template as the standard in each office; keep the core house style for fonts, colours, logos and heading styles the same; allow local changes to the text language and the date format; store the styles in one shared template so that every office starts from the same styles; check that each printer uses the set paper size.
parts.working: Up to 5 marks, 1 mark each for: a common paper size or local page setup; core styles kept the same in all offices; allowed local changes (language, date format); one shared template; printer or paper check.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the steps to set a hanging indent of 0.8 cm for a numbered list style called Terms-list, so that each number sits at the left margin and the text wraps 0.8 cm in.
parts.answer: Open the paragraph settings for Terms-list; in Indentation choose Special: Hanging and enter 0.8 cm, with the left indent set to 0.8 cm; keep the number at the margin with a tab stop at 0.8 cm if needed; click OK and update the style.
parts.working: 1 mark: open the paragraph settings for the style. 1 mark: left indent 0.8 cm. 1 mark: hanging indent of 0.8 cm (first line at 0). 1 mark: updating or applying the style so the list follows it.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a header and a footer in a document.
parts.answer: A header is an area in the top margin of each page; a footer is an area in the bottom margin; text or fields placed in them appear automatically on every page (of the section).
parts.working: B1 header top margin / footer bottom margin. B1 repeated on every page.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two items commonly placed in a footer.
parts.answer: Any two: page number; total number of pages; file name/path; date; author's name; copyright notice; company contact details.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why automated fields, rather than typed text, should be used for the page number and date in a header.
parts.answer: Automated fields update automatically – page numbers change when pages are added or removed and the date updates each time the document is opened/printed – so they are always correct without the user retyping them.
parts.working: B1 updates automatically. B1 example: page numbering after edits / current date when printed.

practice.stem: A document's header has a centre tab and a right tab. The page is A4 portrait (21.0 cm wide). The margins are changed to 2.5 cm on the left and 2.5 cm on the right.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate where, measured from the left margin, the right tab stop must be placed so that the right-aligned item lines up with the right margin.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate where the centre tab stop must be placed, measured from the left margin.
parts.answer: 8.0 cm

practice.stem: The footer of a 23-page leaflet uses automated fields to show 'Page X of Y'.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what the footer shows on the seventh page.
parts.answer: Page 7 of 23
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Two extra pages are added in the middle of the leaflet. State what the footer now shows on the last page.
parts.answer: Page 25 of 25
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A spreadsheet records rainfall for ten cities in Pakistan. Before printing, you are told to place your name, centre number and candidate number in the header, and an automated file path in the footer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the automated file path is useful on the printout.
parts.answer: It shows exactly where the file is saved (drive, folders and file name), so it can be found again.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two other automated fields that can be inserted into a spreadsheet header or footer.
parts.answer: Any two: page number; number of pages; date; time; file name; sheet (tab) name.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State two reasons why an office might require the file name to appear in the footer of every printed document.
parts.answer: Any two: so the electronic copy can be found quickly; to identify which version of the document was printed; helps if pages from different documents get mixed up; consistency with house style.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between a header and a heading.
parts.answer: A header is text placed in the top margin that repeats on every page; a heading is a title within the body text that introduces a section and appears only once where it is typed.
parts.working: B1 header – top margin, every page. B1 heading – in the body, introduces a section, appears once.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between a footnote and a footer.
parts.answer: A footnote gives extra information or a reference linked to a numbered mark in the text and appears at the bottom of the page where the mark is; a footer holds the same items (e.g. page number) on every page.
parts.working: B1 footnote linked to a reference mark/specific text. B1 footer repeated on every page.

practice.stem: A three-page letter from a law firm in Karachi must show the words 'Private and Confidential' at the top of every page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State where the words 'Private and Confidential' should be placed so that they appear on every page.
parts.answer: In the header.
parts.working: B1 header (not typed at the top of the body text).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why these words should be typed as ordinary text rather than inserted as an automated field.
parts.answer: The words never change, so they are fixed text; automated fields are only needed for information that changes, such as the date or page number.
parts.working: B1 text is fixed/does not change; fields are for changing data (date, page number, file name).

practice.stem: After finishing a document, a student checks the header and footer before printing.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State three things the student should check.
parts.answer: Any three: all required items are present (e.g. name, date, page number); items are in the correct position/alignment and line up with the margins; fields are automated, not typed; spelling of typed text is correct; they appear on every page required (or not on the first page if set); no extra text has been added.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name the automated field you would insert into a footer to show each of these.
(i) the total number of pages in the document
(ii) the name of the file and the folder it is saved in
(iii) today's date, updated each time the document is opened or printed
parts.answer: (i) number of pages (total pages / NumPages) field (ii) file name and path field (iii) date field (set to update automatically)
parts.working: 1 mark each. Accept the generic field names.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A tour company in Skardu produces a 12-page brochure. The text '© Baltoro Treks 2026' must appear on every page. State whether it should be placed in the header or the footer and give a reason.
parts.answer: In the footer, because copyright and legal notices are usually small and at the bottom of each page, where they do not distract from the main content but are on every page.
parts.working: 1 mark: footer. 1 mark: appears on every page / does not distract from content at the top.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the copyright text is entered once in the footer rather than typed at the bottom of each page.
parts.answer: It is typed only once and automatically appears in the same place on every page, even if pages are added or text moves.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A header must show a school's name on the left, the report title in the centre and the page number on the right, all on the same line. Describe two ways of placing the three items without using spaces.
parts.answer: Use a centre tab stop and a right tab stop (at the centre and right margin) and press Tab between items; or insert a borderless table with three cells, aligning the cells left, centre and right.
parts.working: 1 mark each method.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why spaces should not be used to position the items.
parts.answer: Spaces do not line up exactly (proportional fonts), and the items move if the text, font or margins change, so they will not stay aligned.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student prints a 6-page document and finds that the header appears on page 1 only. Give two possible reasons for this.
parts.answer: e.g. the text was typed at the top of page 1 in the body, not in the header area; 'different first page' was set and the header was added only to the first-page header; the document has section breaks and the header was added to the first section only (not linked).
parts.working: 1 mark each for any two.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student adds a header to a spreadsheet but cannot see it on the screen while editing the cells. Explain why, and state how the student can check the header before printing.
parts.answer: In normal view headers and footers are not shown because they are part of the printed page, not the cells; use page layout view or print preview.
parts.working: 1 mark reason. 1 mark view.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In presentation software, a student adds the slide number and footer text and clicks 'Apply' instead of 'Apply to All'. State what will happen.
parts.answer: The slide number and footer appear only on the selected (current) slide, not on the other slides.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State how the student can make the footer appear on every slide.
parts.answer: Click 'Apply to All' (or add it on the master slide).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student's header reads: 'Report on Rainfall – Hassan Ali – 28/10/2026 – Page 3'. Everything was typed by hand. Identify the two items that should have been automated fields and explain why.
parts.answer: The date and the page number. A typed page number would be '3' on every page / wrong when pages change; a typed date would not update. Automated fields update by themselves, so they are always correct.
parts.working: 1 mark each item. 1 mark reason (fields update automatically/correct on every page).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two reasons why page numbers are useful in a printed 30-page report.
parts.answer: Any two, e.g. the reader can find a section using the contents page; pages can be put back in order if dropped or separated; people can refer to a particular page in a meeting; the reader can see that no page is missing.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A practical task says your name, centre number and candidate number must be in the header of a spreadsheet printout. Explain why you should not type them into cells in row 1 of the worksheet instead.
parts.answer: Data in row 1 prints only on the first page, not on every page; it also becomes part of the data, so it could affect sorting, formulas or a chart range.
parts.working: 1 mark: not on every page. 1 mark: interferes with the data (sorting/formulas/ranges) / is not in the header as asked.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A company in Dubai sends reports to offices in Pakistan and the USA. The date field in the footer shows 03/04/2027. Explain why this can cause confusion.
parts.answer: It could be read as 3 April (day/month) or as 4 March (month/day in the USA).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest a better format for the date field and give an example.
parts.answer: A format with the month in words, e.g. 3 April 2027 (or 2027-04-03).
parts.working: 1 mark.

practice.stem:
You are working on a report for a solar-panel company in Lahore. The page is A4 portrait with 2 cm margins. The instructions say:
• in the header: your name left aligned, and an automated date right aligned
• in the footer: an automated file name centred, and an automated page number right aligned
• no other text in the header or footer

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the steps to place the automated date at the right of the header.
parts.answer: Open/edit the header, move to the right-hand position (right tab stop at the right margin or right-align), then insert a date field set to update automatically.
parts.working: B1 open header and right align / right tab at margin. B1 insert date field (update automatically).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the right-aligned items must line up with the right margin of the page.
parts.answer: The house style requires header/footer items to align with the margins of the body text; if the tab stop is beyond or short of the margin, it will not match the text and will look unprofessional/be marked wrong.
parts.working: B1 consistent alignment with body margins.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the type of field that should be used to show the file name in the footer.
parts.answer: An automated file name field (inserted from the field list, not typed).
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A school annual report has a cover page followed by 18 pages of content. The cover must not show a header, footer or page number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the header and footer setting that removes them from the cover only.
parts.answer: Different first page.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: The first content page must show page number 1. Describe how this is achieved.
parts.answer: Format the page numbers to start at 0 for the cover (so the next page is 1), or put a next-page section break after the cover and set page numbering in the new section to start at 1.
parts.working: B1 page number format / start at. B1 correct start value (0 on cover, or 1 in new section after break).

practice.stem: A project file has 26 pages. Pages 1 and 2 are the title page and contents page and must not be numbered. Page numbering starts at 1 on page 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the page number printed on the last page.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The footer shows 'Page X of Y', where Y is the total number of numbered pages. Write the footer that appears on the 10th physical page.
parts.answer: Page 8 of 24

practice.stem: A presentation about water conservation for a Year 8 class has 15 slides. Slide numbers and the presenter's name must appear in the footer of every slide except the title slide.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the footer items should be set on the master slide.
parts.answer: Items placed on the master slide appear on every slide automatically in the same position and style, so they are consistent and only need to be added once (and changed once).
parts.working: B1 appears on all slides. B1 consistent / saves time / one change updates all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the setting that stops the footer showing on the title slide.
parts.answer: Don't show on title slide.
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A clinic in Quetta wants a letter template. The clinic's name and logo must be at the top of every page, and the address, phone number and website at the bottom of every page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the clinic should use a header and footer for these items rather than typing them at the top and bottom of the body text.
parts.answer: Header/footer content repeats automatically on every page and stays in the same place even when the body text is edited or extends to more pages; text typed in the body would move with the text and only appear on the first page.
parts.working: B1 repeats on every page. B1 does not move when body text changes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest one setting that keeps the contact details on the first page only, if the clinic decides later pages need only a page number.
parts.answer: Different first page (with the contact details in the first-page footer and a page number in the other pages' footer).
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A spreadsheet of monthly sales for a shoe shop in Sialkot must be printed showing the formulas, on a single landscape page, with your name in the header and the page number in the footer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: List three print/page settings that must be made, apart from the header and footer.
parts.answer: Any three: show formulas (formula view); landscape orientation; fit to one page wide/one page; show row and column headings; gridlines if required; columns widened so formulas are fully visible.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the column widths should be checked before printing the formulas.
parts.answer: Formulas are often longer than their values, so narrow columns would cut them off and they could not be read in full.
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: Five students in a group each write a chapter of a project about Pakistan's renewable energy. The chapters will be combined into one file.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain two problems that could occur in the headers and footers when the chapters are combined, and how they can be avoided.
parts.answer: Any two: different fonts/sizes/alignment in each student's header – agree a template/house style for headers and footers; typed page numbers restart or are wrong – use automated page number fields after combining; different information in each header – decide content beforehand; section breaks carried in may stop headers continuing – check 'link to previous'.
parts.working: For each: 1 mark problem, 1 mark solution.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two reasons why the text in headers and footers is usually smaller and less prominent than the body text.
parts.answer: Any two: it is supporting information, not the main content; so it does not distract the reader from the body text; it must fit in the margin area; consistent professional appearance / house style.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A user types '1' at the bottom of page 1, '2' at the bottom of page 2 and so on in a 10-page document instead of using a page number field. Describe two problems this may cause.
parts.answer: Any two: if text is added or deleted, the numbers move to the wrong position on the page (into the middle of a page); numbers will be wrong if pages are added/removed and must be retyped; takes much longer; inconsistent position/format.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

practice.stem: A 40-page guide to the Karakoram Highway has five chapters. Each page header must show the name of the chapter it is in.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the type of break that must be inserted at the start of each new chapter (chapters 2 to 5).
parts.answer: A section break (next page).
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Chapter 1 starts on page 1. State how many of these breaks are needed and how many sections the document then has.
parts.answer: 4 section breaks; 5 sections.
parts.working: One break before each of chapters 2–5 = 4 breaks; sections = breaks + 1 = 5. B1 both.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe what must be done in the header of chapters 2 to 5 before typing the new chapter name.
parts.answer: Turn off 'link to previous' so the header is not the same as the previous section's.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A presenter in Karachi prepares slides for a conference on 15 March 2027. She is preparing them in February. The date in the slide footer can be 'fixed' or 'update automatically'. State which option she should choose and explain why.
parts.answer: Fixed, set to 15 March 2027, because the slides are about the conference day; an automatic date would show the date the slides are opened or printed, e.g. a February date.
parts.working: 1 mark: fixed. 1 mark: reason.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one example of a presentation where the 'update automatically' option would be better.
parts.answer: e.g. a weekly sales update or a daily notice screen that is shown again and again and should always show the current date.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A house style says the footer must show the file name. A student typed 'report.rtf' in the footer, then saved the work as 'Hassan_report' in the word processor's own format. Explain the problem and how it should have been avoided.
parts.answer: The footer still shows 'report.rtf', which is now the wrong file name. An automated file name field should have been inserted; it shows the current file name and updates when the file is saved under a new name (after the field is updated or the document printed).
parts.working: 1 mark: typed name now wrong. 1 mark: use an automated file name field. 1 mark: field changes to match the new name.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A spreadsheet file has three worksheets: Sales, Costs and Summary. A student adds a header to the Sales sheet, then prints all three sheets. Only the Sales printout has the header. Explain why.
parts.answer: Each worksheet has its own page settings, including header and footer; adding a header to one sheet does not add it to the others.
parts.working: 1 mark: header belongs to one sheet. 1 mark: each sheet has separate page setup.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how the student can add the same header to all three sheets at once.
parts.answer: Select (group) all three sheets, e.g. right-click a sheet tab and choose Select All Sheets, then add the header in page setup; ungroup afterwards.
parts.working: 1 mark: select/group all sheets. 1 mark: then set the header once.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student pressed Enter many times to move a heading to the top of a new page. The document now has a blank page in it. The footer uses fields to show 'Page X of Y'. Explain how the blank page affects the footer.
parts.answer: The blank page counts as a page, so Y (the total) is one too many and every page after it has a page number one higher than expected.
parts.working: 1 mark: total pages increased. 1 mark: later page numbers shift by one.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the correct way to start the heading on a new page.
parts.answer: Delete the extra blank lines and insert a page break before the heading (or set 'page break before' in the heading style).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher prints handouts of a presentation, with three slides on each page. She wants the school name at the top of every handout page. Explain why she cannot use the slide footer for this.
parts.answer: The slide footer appears on each slide image, not at the top of the printed handout page; slides have no header, so a header must be set for the notes and handouts instead.
parts.working: 1 mark: slide footer is on the slides themselves. 1 mark: handouts have their own header/footer settings.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one other item that could be added automatically to the handout footer.
parts.answer: e.g. page number, date, or footer text such as the teacher's name.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The footer of a spreadsheet contains an automated file path field. The file is saved in a folder called Rainfall on the C: drive, then copied to a USB drive (E:) and printed from there. State what change will be seen in the footer and explain why.
parts.answer: The path will start with E: (the USB drive) instead of C:, because the field shows where the file is saved at the time it is printed.
parts.working: 1 mark: path changes to the USB location. 1 mark: field updates automatically.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student's report is printed on one side of the paper only. The option 'different odd and even pages' has been ticked by mistake. Describe what the student will see when the report is printed, and explain why.
parts.answer: Only the odd-numbered pages show the header/footer (or the even pages show a different one), because with this option on, even pages use a separate, empty header and footer.
parts.working: 1 mark: even pages missing/different header or footer. 1 mark: separate even-page header/footer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A spreadsheet must be printed with your name on the left of the header and an automated date on the right of the header, and the automated sheet name in the centre of the footer. Describe the steps.
parts.answer: Open page setup (or page layout view) and choose header/footer; click the left section of the header and type your name; click the right section of the header and insert the date field; go to the footer, click the centre section and insert the sheet name field; check in print preview.
parts.working: 1 mark each for: opening header/footer settings; name in left header section; date field in right header section; sheet name field in centre footer section.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain one difference between adding a header in a word processor and adding header-type information in presentation software.
parts.answer: In a word processor any text, fields or images can be placed in a header at the top of every page; on presentation slides there is no header area – only a footer, date and slide number (set for all slides on the master), although handouts and notes pages can have a header.
parts.working: 1 mark: word processor header at top of every page. 1 mark: slides use footer/date/slide number only (header only for handouts/notes).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A newsletter for a hockey club in Sialkot is set in two columns. The club name is in the header. State whether the header text runs across both columns or stays in one column, and explain why.
parts.answer: It runs across the full width of the page between the margins, because column settings apply only to the body text; the header is a separate area at the top of the page.
parts.working: 1 mark: full width. 1 mark: columns affect body text only.

practice.stem: A report is changed to A4 landscape (29.7 cm wide) with a left margin of 2.0 cm and a right margin of 1.5 cm. The header's tab stops were set for portrait pages at 8.75 cm (centre) and 17.5 cm (right), which matched the portrait text width with the same margins.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the new positions, measured from the left margin, for the centre and right tab stops.
parts.answer: Centre 13.1 cm; right 26.2 cm.
parts.working: M1 text width 29.7 − 2.0 − 1.5 = 26.2 cm. A1 centre 13.1 cm, right 26.2 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe what will appear wrong in the header if the tab stops are not changed.
parts.answer: The 'right-aligned' item would end at 17.5 cm, well short of the right margin, and the centred item would not be in the centre of the page.
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A novel by a writer in Karachi is printed double-sided as a book. The book title must appear at the top left of even-numbered (left-hand) pages, and the chapter title at the top right of odd-numbered (right-hand) pages. Page numbers appear on the outside edge of each page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the header setting needed so that odd and even pages can have different headers.
parts.answer: Different odd and even pages.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: State where the page number should be aligned on odd pages and on even pages.
parts.answer: Odd (right-hand) pages: right aligned. Even (left-hand) pages: left aligned.
parts.working: B1 each.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why each chapter must be in a separate section for the chapter title to change.
parts.answer: Header content is the same throughout a section; a section break at each chapter allows a different header, once it is unlinked from the previous section ('link to previous' turned off).
parts.working: B1 headers apply per section. B1 unlink from previous / new section per chapter.

practice.stem: A database report lists all students in a school sports club, grouped by house. You must add a report title, page numbers, the house name before each group, and a count of all students at the end of the report.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the section of the report in which each item should be placed:
(i) the report title shown once at the start
(ii) the page numbers
(iii) the total count shown once at the end
parts.answer: (i) report header; (ii) page footer (or page header); (iii) report footer.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between the report header and the page header.
parts.answer: The report header appears once at the start of the report (first page only); the page header appears at the top of every page.
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A letter has a top margin of 3.0 cm. The header starts 1.25 cm from the top edge of the page. The header contains a logo.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the greatest height the logo can have without pushing into the body text area.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The original logo is 6.0 cm wide and 2.4 cm high. Calculate the largest width it can have, with its aspect ratio maintained, so that it fits this height. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

practice.stem: A legal contract was signed on 3 March. The contract document has a date field in the header that updates automatically. It is reprinted on 10 June.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the date shown in the header of the reprinted copy and explain why this is a problem.
parts.answer: 10 June – the automatic field shows the current date, so the header no longer shows the date of signing and could cause confusion about when the contract was agreed.
parts.working: B1 10 June. B1 problem explained.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how the header should have been set up.
parts.answer: Insert the date as fixed text / a date field set not to update automatically (or type the signing date).
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A university thesis has 6 introductory pages (title, declaration, acknowledgements, abstract, contents and list of tables) before Chapter 1. The introductory pages must be numbered i, ii, iii …, and Chapter 1 must start at page 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how to set up the page numbering.
parts.answer: Insert a next-page section break before Chapter 1; in the first section set the page number format to lower-case Roman numerals (i, ii, iii); in the second section unlink the footer from the previous section, choose Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3) and set numbering to start at 1.
parts.working: B1 section break. B1 Roman numeral format in section 1. B1 Arabic format starting at 1 in section 2 (unlinked).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the page number printed on the abstract, which is the fourth introductory page.
parts.answer: iv
parts.working: B1

practice.stem: A portrait report contains one landscape page holding a wide table of exam statistics. After changing that page to landscape, the student notices that the right-aligned page number in the footer of the landscape page is now in the middle of the page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why this has happened.
parts.answer: The footer's right tab stop is still at the position set for the narrower portrait page, so on the wider landscape page it is no longer at the right margin.
parts.working: B1 tab/alignment set for portrait width. B1 landscape text width is greater.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how to correct it without affecting the portrait pages.
parts.answer: In the landscape section, unlink the footer from the previous section and move the right tab stop to the new right margin (or use right alignment).
parts.working: B1 unlink from previous section. B1 move tab to new right margin.

practice.stem: A database report lists 48 orders for a bakery in Hyderabad, sorted by delivery date, with a calculated Total column for each order. The report runs over 3 pages.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The manager wants the overall sum of all order totals shown once at the end. State where this calculation should be placed.
parts.answer: In the report footer.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what would happen if the sum calculation were placed in the page footer instead.
parts.answer: It would be printed at the bottom of every page, and depending on the software it may show only that page's total or repeat the overall total, so the report would be confusing/incorrect.
parts.working: B1 appears on every page. B1 gives page/partial totals or repeated values – not a single overall total.

parts.label: c
parts.text: On average, how many orders appear on each page if the orders are split as evenly as possible?

practice.stem: An examination board requires candidates to put their name, centre number and candidate number in the header of every printed page of practical work.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the details are required on every page rather than only on the first page.
parts.answer: Pages can become separated or mixed with other candidates' work; having the details on each page means every page can be identified and returned to the right candidate.
parts.working: B1 pages may be separated. B1 each page identifiable.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why using the header is better than typing these details at the top of the body text on each page.
parts.answer: The header repeats automatically on every page and stays in place if the body text is edited; typing on each page is slow and the text would move as content changes.
parts.working: B1 automatic repetition. B1 fixed position / saves time.

practice.stem: A workbook for a cricket academy in Rawalpindi has three sheets named Batting, Bowling and Fielding. Each sheet is printed on two pages. The footer must show the sheet name on the left and 'Page X of Y' on the right, where Y counts the pages of that sheet only.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the sheet name should be an automated field rather than typed text.
parts.answer: If a sheet is renamed, or the header/footer is copied to other sheets, the field shows the correct name automatically.
parts.working: B1

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the footer text printed on the second page of the Bowling sheet.
parts.answer: Bowling (left) and Page 2 of 2 (right).
parts.working: B1

parts.label: c
parts.text: If all three sheets were instead printed as one job with continuous page numbering, state the footer on the second page of the Bowling sheet.
parts.answer: Bowling (left) and Page 4 of 6 (right).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A spreadsheet of 400 sales records prints on 9 pages. On pages 2 to 9 the column headings in row 1 are missing, so it is hard to tell which column is which. A student suggests putting the column headings in the header. Explain why this is not a good solution.
parts.answer: The header is separate from the cells, so the headings would not line up exactly with the columns (and would not change if column widths change); the header should hold document details such as the name and date.
parts.working: 1 mark: headings would not line up with the columns. 1 mark: header is for page information / would not adjust.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the setting that should be used instead.
parts.answer: In page setup, set row 1 as the rows to repeat at the top of each page (print titles); the column headings then print above the columns on every page.
parts.working: 1 mark: rows to repeat at top / print titles. 1 mark: row 1 printed at top of every page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A report has three sections separated by section breaks. A student edits the header in section 3 to show 'Appendix', but the headers in sections 1 and 2 also change to 'Appendix'. Explain why this happened.
parts.answer: The headers of the sections are linked to the previous section (link to previous is on by default), so a change in one section's header is copied to the linked sections.
parts.working: 1 mark: headers linked to previous. 1 mark: change applied to all linked sections.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how to give section 3 its own header without changing sections 1 and 2.
parts.answer: Restore the earlier headers; in section 3's header turn off 'link to previous', then type 'Appendix' in the section 3 header only.
parts.working: 1 mark: turn off link to previous in section 3. 1 mark: then edit only that header.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A report is set to A4 landscape (29.7 cm wide) with a left margin of 2.2 cm and a right margin of 1.9 cm. The header uses a borderless table with three equal columns that fill the width between the margins. Calculate the width of each column, correct to 2 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the alignment needed in each cell so that the items appear at the left margin, centre and right margin.
parts.answer: Left cell left-aligned, middle cell centred, right cell right-aligned.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A company's letters have an author field in the footer that shows the author name from the document properties. Amna writes each new letter by opening an old letter written by Imran, changing the text and saving it under a new name. Her letters show the name 'Imran'. Explain why this happens.
parts.answer: The field displays the author stored in the document's properties; saving Imran's file under a new name keeps its properties, so the author is still Imran.
parts.working: 1 mark: field reads the document properties. 1 mark: properties copied from Imran's file are not changed by Save As.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest two ways to make sure the correct author is shown.
parts.answer: e.g. change the author in the document properties before printing; start each letter as a new document from a template so the current user's name is used; set her own user name in the software; check the footer in print preview.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student creates a new document, inserts a file name field in the footer, and prints immediately without saving. The footer shows 'Document1'. Explain why.
parts.answer: The document has not been saved, so it has no real file name yet; the software's temporary default name is shown.
parts.working: 1 mark: not saved. 1 mark: default/temporary name used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe what the student must do so that the correct file name is printed.
parts.answer: Save the document with the required file name (in the required format), then update the field (or check print preview) so it shows the new name, then print.
parts.working: 1 mark: save with correct name. 1 mark: update field before printing.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Word processors offer different date fields. For each requirement, state which date should be shown and whether it should change.
(i) The date a contract was written, which must never change.
(ii) The date a copy of a price list was printed, so customers know how current it is.
(iii) The date a shared report was last edited.
parts.answer: (i) a fixed date / the date the document was created (does not update) (ii) the print date (updates each time it is printed) (iii) the date last saved (updates whenever the document is saved)
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A 4-page letter from a bank in Lahore must show the full letterhead (logo, address and phone number) in the header of page 1 only. Pages 2 to 4 must show a smaller header with the customer's name, the date and the page number. Describe how to set this up.
parts.answer: Turn on 'different first page'; put the logo, address and phone number in the first-page header; in the header for the other pages insert the customer's name, an automated date and a page number field; check pages 2 to 4 show the smaller header and page 1 the letterhead.
parts.working: 1 mark: different first page. 1 mark: letterhead in first-page header. 1 mark: customer name and date in second header. 1 mark: page number field in second header.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State how many pages show the smaller header if the letter grows to 7 pages.
parts.working: All pages except page 1: 7 − 1 = 6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A health charity in Quetta prints a two-page leaflet for the public. The designer wants to leave out the header and footer. Discuss whether a header and footer should be used on this leaflet.
parts.answer: For: a footer could hold the charity's name, contact details and date of issue, so readers know who produced it and if it is up to date; page numbers or 'continued overleaf' help if the pages are separated. Against: with only two pages page numbers are hardly needed; headers take space from the main content and may make a public leaflet look like a formal report; the charity name may already be in the title. Conclusion, e.g. use a small footer with contact details and date, but no header.
parts.working: Up to 2 marks for points for, up to 2 marks for points against; a reasoned conclusion is needed for full marks (max 4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A database report lists 95 student records. The report header with the title appears only on the first page, so page 1 has room for 25 records and every other page for 30 records. Calculate how many pages the report will have.
parts.answer: 4 pages
parts.working: M1: 95 − 25 = 70 records after page 1; 70 ÷ 30 = 2.33, so 3 more pages. A1: 1 + 3 = 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The page footer contains fields to show 'Page X of Y'. State what it shows on the last page.
parts.answer: Page 4 of 4
parts.working: 1 mark (follow through).

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the section of the report where the column headings should be placed so they appear at the top of every page.
parts.answer: The page header.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A wide spreadsheet prints as 6 pages: 3 pages across and 2 pages down. The footer shows the page number. With the page order set to 'down, then over', state the page number printed on the page that holds the middle columns of the bottom rows.
parts.working: Down, then over: column 1 of pages is 1–2, column 2 is 3–4, column 3 is 5–6; middle bottom = 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The page order is changed to 'over, then down'. State the new page number of the same page.
parts.working: Over, then down: top row 1–3, bottom row 4–6; middle bottom = 5.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why automated page numbers are essential when a spreadsheet prints over several pages like this.
parts.answer: The pages must be put together in the right order to read the whole sheet; the numbers update automatically if the print area, scaling or page order change, so they are always correct.
parts.working: 1 mark: helps arrange pages in order. 1 mark: numbers update automatically when the layout changes.
